subject: Stakeholder acceptance sherpa: MAP, exit tests, and pilot close checklist
messages:

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>

Subject: MAP and acceptance criteria for pilot (HealthTech)

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Raj and I walked away excited but we need to line up a crisp mutual action plan and a short list of acceptance tests so our legal and security teams can sign off on the pilot. Can you send a short MAP that includes:
- Concrete success metrics (latency, accuracy, throughput)
- Clear exit gates (what causes a stop or rollback)
- Minimal acceptance tests we can run in our UAT environment

We also have a security questionnaire — I attached the version we typically push to vendors. Would appreciate a one-page checklist if possible.

Best,
Samantha

Attachment: HT-SEC-Q_20261020.pdf (pdf)
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T11:02:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP and acceptance criteria for pilot (HealthTech)

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear ask and the questionnaire. Uploaded a first-pass MAP and a compact acceptance-tests doc to the shared Drive (link below). Key highlights here:

Summary MAP (v0.3 attached)
- Objective: Validate Redwood inference for clinical-notes summarization at 95% AU-recall on the evaluation set and median inference p95 latency <= 180ms for 512-token runs.
- Success signals: 95% AU-recall OR F1 >= 0.88 on the curated test set; p95 latency <= 180ms in your UAT profile; token cost per 1k <= $0.90 (estimate).
- Exit gates: accuracy drop > 4 percentage points vs. baseline OR p95 latency increase > 25% sustained over 24h OR any verified PII leakage event.
- Acceptance tests (minimal): 1) 1000-sample concordance sweep (black-box) 2) latency profile (synthetic concurrency 10) 3) KV-cache warmup smoke 4) reranking sanity checks.

I've attached the MAP spreadsheet and a short markdown with test steps. Karthik — I flagged a few quant/latency knobs where we might recommend 8-bit quant + batch=8 for cost/latency balance; can you confirm the safe perf envelope? Grace — proposed timeline below assumes two-week UAT (start 10/25).

Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMAPs
Attachments: MAP-v0.3.xlsx, pilot-acceptance-tests.md

—Irene
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Samantha Lopez <samantha.lopez@healthtech.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T08:47:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP and acceptance criteria for pilot (HealthTech)

Samantha / Irene — quick tech note from my side on the perf envelope:
- Safe defaults: 8-bit quantized variant + model shard over 2 GPUs yields p95 around 140–170ms at batch=8 for 512 tokens on our benchmark.
- Stress test: if you spike concurrency to 25 with the same model variant you should expect p95 to rise toward ~260ms; that's why we put the 25% sustained increase exit gate.
- Acceptance-test details: for the latency profile, run three 30-minute windows at target concurrency (10) during different times of day to capture jitter. Include cold-cache and warm-cache runs.

I recommend we also add a quality-stability test: run the concordance sweep nightly and fail the gate if rolling 3-day average drops >2 pts.

Happy to be on the call to run the smoke tests — tell me a window.

—Karthik
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lopez <samantha.lopez@healthtech.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-23T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: MAP and acceptance criteria for pilot (HealthTech)

Hi team — proposed pilot timeline and responsibilities (short):
- 10/25: UAT environment handed over by HealthTech (data slices and test accounts)
- 10/26–11/08: Run acceptance tests (concordance sweep + latency windows + security checklist)
- 11/09: Stakeholder review meeting (decision: go/no-go to cutover to limited prod)

Internal owners: Redwood runs the acceptance-tests harness (Karthik) and provides daily KPIs to HealthTech slack channel. Samantha / Raj: validate functional correctness and sign the sign-off doc.

Note on rollback: If an exit gate trips during the UAT, we pause and perform a 24h remediation window; if unresolved we execute rollback to baseline model and re-run the nightly concordance sweep before rescheduling the review.

Grace
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Lopez <samantha.lopez@healthtech.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Thanks — this looks good and concrete. Raj and I reviewed the MAP-v0.3 and pilot-acceptance-tests.md. Two quick asks before the 10/25 handoff:
1) Can you add a one-page security response that maps the HT questionnaire items to Redwood artifacts (SOC2 scope, audit logs, KMS notes)?
2) Can we shorten the nightly concordance sweep to a 500-sample quick-pass for the first two nights to surface major regressions faster?

We'll upload the UAT data slice and test accounts to the Drive folder tonight. If you can confirm the security mapping by EOD tomorrow and agree to the shortened early sweep, we can start 10/25.

Thanks — Samantha
VP Product, HealthTech Solutions
